The Cat and Fiddle: England's Most Famous Biking Road

The A537 from Macclesfield to Buxton — known universally as the Cat and Fiddle Road — is arguably the most famous motorcycle road in England. For decades it has drawn riders from across the country to its sweeping moorland bends and panoramic views. It's also one of the most contentious, with a history of accidents that led to significant safety measures.

The Road

The Cat and Fiddle Road runs for 7.5 miles across the high moorland between Macclesfield and Buxton in the Peak District. It climbs from Macclesfield to the Cat and Fiddle Inn at 515 metres — the second-highest pub in England — then descends to Buxton. The road features a succession of flowing bends, with panoramic views across the Cheshire Plain to the west and the Peak District to the east.

What Makes It Special

The Cat and Fiddle's appeal lies in its combination of fast, flowing bends and dramatic open scenery. The road rises above the treeline onto exposed moorland where the views stretch for miles. The bends are well-sighted and smoothly profiled — designed for flowing, progressive riding rather than tight, technical work. On a dry day with clear views, it's motorcycling perfection.

Safety and Speed Cameras

The road was once statistically the most dangerous road in Britain, with a disproportionate number of motorcycle accidents. In response, Cheshire East Council installed average speed cameras along the entire length, enforcing the 50mph speed limit. These cameras have dramatically reduced accidents and transformed the riding experience. The road is now much safer but no less enjoyable when ridden within the limit.

The cameras actually improved the Cat and Fiddle experience. Riders now flow through the bends at a consistent pace rather than racing. The road rewards smooth riding perfectly.

Best Time to Ride

The Cat and Fiddle is busiest at weekends from spring to autumn. Midweek mornings offer the quietest conditions. The road is often closed or hazardous in winter due to ice and snow — the exposed moorland sees some of the worst winter weather in England. Visibility can drop suddenly in fog, which rolls in off the moors without warning.

The Loop

Combine the Cat and Fiddle with the A54 through Allgreave and the A523 back to Macclesfield for a 30-mile loop that includes varied riding. Alternatively, continue from Buxton over the A53 to Leek for views of the Roaches — a dramatic gritstone escarpment. Several cafes in Buxton and Macclesfield serve as meeting points for riders.

Practical Tips

  • Speed limit: 50mph (average speed cameras throughout)
  • Fuel: Macclesfield and Buxton both have plenty of fuel stations
  • The pub: Cat and Fiddle Inn — reopened and welcoming riders again
  • Surface: Generally excellent, but watch for standing water and mud from farm vehicles
